Ein Leserbrief / Uma carta de leitor: Ein Leserbrief / A letter to the editor
Prezada redação, no seu jornal foi notic: Dear editors, your newspaper reported last week that the city wants to spend less money on cycle lanes. I am of the opinion that this would be a mistake. Firstly, more and more people cycle to work to save time and money. Secondly, cycling is good for the environment and for your health. Although cars are important in the city, we need safe routes for cyclists. If the city invested more, more people could do without a car. Yours faithfully, Maria Becker
— Bom dia, aqui é Tom Weber. Gostaria de: — Good morning, this is Tom Weber. I would like to reschedule my appointment on Tuesday.
— Não há problema. Quando seria bom para: — No problem. When would suit you?
— Se possível, na quinta. Na terça preci: — If possible, on Thursday. On Tuesday I have to go to an important meeting.
— Na quinta às dez ainda teríamos um hor: — On Thursday at ten we would still have a free slot.
— Serve muito bem. A senhora poderia me: — That suits me very well. Could you send me a confirmation, please?
— Naturalmente. O e-mail será enviado ai: — Of course. The e-mail will be sent today.

Os 14 erros mais comuns do B1: The 14 most common B1 mistakes for English speakers
Leia cada par em voz alta: primeiro o er: Read each pair out loud: first the wrong one, then the right one. Most of them come from copying English word order or English prepositions.
Depois da subordinada, a principal começ: After the subordinate clause, the main clause starts with the verb (English keeps "I go"; German says «gehe ich»).
Depois de «trotzdem», o verbo na 2ª posi: After «trotzdem» ("nevertheless"), the verb is in 2nd position — unlike English "Nevertheless I go".
«zu» goes between the prefix and the verb.
In «um … zu», you do not repeat the subject (English "in order to work", not "in order I to work").
Fixed preposition: «warten auf» — not «für», even though English says "wait FOR".
The relative pronoun agrees in gender.
After «alles»: «was» (English "everything that" tempts you to say «das»).
Present tense: «wenn» — even though English says "when".
Depois de «weil», o verbo vai para o fim: After «weil», the verb goes to the end.
Adjective used as a noun: capital letter.
